name: The Floor: costing and revenue package
units: USD billions per year, 2025 dollars, at full operation (year 8 of the transition) unless stated

pillars.name: Medical care
pillars.design: One public payer covering every resident, no premiums, deductibles or copays; provider rates between Medicare and today's private average; global hospital budgets; negotiated drug prices; dental, vision, hearing; long-term care phased in from year six.
pillars.basis: CBO Working Paper 2020-08 options 3 and 4, scaled to CMS NHE 2024

pillars.name: Housing
pillars.design: Housing First for everyone homeless; a rent guarantee so no household pays more than 30% of income for a modest home, as an entitlement; a federal Housing Development Authority building 200,000 permanently affordable homes a year, bond-financed; an owner backstop.

pillars.name: Food
pillars.design: A Floor card every resident holds, loaded with USDA's Thrifty Food Plan, full at or below the poverty line and tapering to zero at 250% of it, no application or conditions; universal free school meals; a food-recovery program.

pillars.name: Education
pillars.design: Tuition- and fee-free public two- and four-year college for residents, first dollar, no income cap; states keep appropriations; Pell becomes a living-cost grant; free short credentials and training; an apprenticeship fund tripling active apprentices; expanded WIOA.

lines.measure: Employer health contribution, 7.5% of payroll above an employer's first $2 million
Household health contribution, 4% of income above $20,000 single / $40,000 joint
State maintenance of effort: the states' Medicaid share paid to the national plan
Top four individual brackets up 2 points
Cap the tax value of itemized deductions at 15%
Wealth tax, 2% above $50 million, 3% above $1 billion
lines.note: after a Penn Wharton-sized avoidance haircut; constitutional risk noted

reserves.measure: Carbon fee, $25 a ton rising 5% a year

transition.principle: Each pillar's benefits switch on only after its revenue is in place

milestones.event: Revenue package enacted; Floor card and food credit live; free school meals; free community college and training; Housing Development Authority chartered; Housing First surge begins; drug prices set and uninsured enrolled
Medicare for everyone under 26 and over 55
Everyone covered; 200,000 public homes a year begins
Zero cost sharing, dental and vision; rent guarantee becomes an entitlement; free four-year public college

macro.hours_worked: 2% to 4% lower, concentrated among caregivers, students, the sick and people over 60
macro.gdp_2030_vs_path: within 1% below to 1.5% above, when financing replaces premiums rather than stacking rates on labor (CBO 2022 single-payer modeling)

key_risks: Provider payment rates: ±300 on the federal health line (the largest uncertainty)
Long-term care timing: +500 federal when it arrives
Wealth tax struck down or avoided: −180 of revenue (fallback: VAT)
Stacked tapers on households just above poverty: fixed by a single Floor taper at about 25 cents on the dollar, +40 to +60
Rent capture before supply arrives; construction labor capacity; health cost growth above GDP if global budgets are not held
State capacity: the program needs an authority that builds, a payer that holds a budget and a tax agency that can run a taper
